D0 Cover — thesis
CAMPFIRE · BANK REC · VECTOR CONCEPT
Concept D — The timeline
Thesis: timing is the root cause. $82,550.00 of the ($82,741.31) difference is two items on the wrong side of the Sep 30 cutoff; the Kestrel wire sat five days in dual approval; check #4098 was voided with a date inside closed August. So the reconciliation is drawn on September as a time axis, bank above, books below, the cutoff as a hard line, and the difference as a track that must go flat.
Where the thesis bends
Only about half of the 14 are really about time. For the bank fee, interest, the FX loss, the AWS transposition and the Datadog duplicate, the date axis is a neutral index, not an explanation; the inspector's weight × score formula carries the reasoning there. Date collisions (Sep 30 has four items on the books side) need a flag layout and a zoom. The month view is for orientation and for seeing done; the week view is where the work happens.
Frames: D1 Hero · D2 Why · D3 Edge · D4 Thread · D5 Many-to-one · D6 Done · D7 Phone. The story runs in order: Maya starts at the cutoff, fixes the opening balance, sweeps left to right, and Daniel approves from his phone.
D1 note
D1
Hero · the month at a glance
Maya opens the month, not a list. The 207 auto-matches are faint grey stitches between the Chase lane and the GL lane. Only the 14 exceptions have colour, and each already carries Ember's proposal as a dashed connector with its confidence.
The shape tells the story before she reads a word: a slant is a date lag (Kestrel), a fan is many-to-one (Cascade), an X is the Gusto row-order trap, a line through the cutoff is timing (Meridian, #4127), the red hook at the left edge is the back-dated void.
The difference track shows where the ($82,741.31) comes from: a plunge at Sep 30 that heals in October's feed. Hence Ember's one suggestion: start at the cutoff.
Trade-off: at month zoom, chips carry the payee only. Amounts arrive on hover or zoom (Z).
D1 note — how to read
How to read the axis
Grey stitch
auto-matched pair; 207 of them form the fabric
Dashed green + %
Ember's proposal and its confidence
Slant
books date differs from bank date
Hollow bead
an entry Ember proposes to create
Capsule past cutoff
expected clearing window (#4127)
Red hook
an entry dated into a closed period
Difference track
unexplained difference by date; flat at $0 means done
D2 note
D2
Why · Meridian crosses the cutoff
'Start there' zooms time to the item's neighbourhood (Sep 23 – Oct 9) and opens the inspector. At ~40 px a day the one-day slant across the cutoff is legible, and the evidence (the Oct 1 live-feed line) is pinned on the axis where it happened instead of in a modal.
The why is a formula, not a vibe: five factors, weight × score, 95.1 → 95%. 'Difference after accept' previews the consequence, which is what makes accepting feel safe. A is accept, X reject, E evidence.
Neighbours stay visible but dimmed; 'Also across the cutoff' queues #4127 next.
Trade-off: the inspector costs 400 px of axis. I zoom rather than squeeze; the header minimap keeps the month in view.
D3 note
D3
Edge · the back-dated void
The beginning-balance problem is drawn where it happened, inside closed August: check #4098 issued 8/21 and cleared 8/26 (grey, reconciled last month), then a void keyed on Sep 12 but dated Aug 28, drawn as a red arc reaching back across the close line. Ember's fix is a hollow bead on Sep 1: reverse the void in the open period.
Daniel's Oct 2 message is already on the item's thread and Ember has answered it. Because the fix touches a closed period, the primary button says what will happen: Accept · send to Daniel.
The difference track switches to this item: a ($1,150.00) gap that starts on Aug 28.
D4 note
D4
Thread · Ember finds the invoice
One thread per transaction, with Ember acting inside it. Maya asks whether an invoice exists; Ember searches the AP inbox and the axis changes live: a dashed 'Bill · NTN-88213' bead appears under the Notion line with a NEW tag, and the inbox arrival shows as an event on Sep 19. The old 72% guess drops to 2 of 2.
Each change Ember made is a row with its own Revert (the read-only search has none). Priya answers in the same thread. The invoice opens in place.
Resolved items stay on the axis as grey checks, so U always has something to click, and the Gusto X is still readable after it is settled.
D5 note
D5
Many-to-one · ⌘-click Cascade
⌘-click the deposit and its three invoices: the fan turns solid and a floating bar sums both sides (61,250.00 = 61,250.00, Δ 0.00, M to match). The inspector lists the selection, Ember agrees at 95%, and the remittance that names all three invoices is right there.
Clustering: at month zoom this is one 'Cascade ×3' chip over a narrow fan; at week zoom the invoices spread within the day so each is clickable.
Northstar's $25 fee and the #4098 reversal wait on Daniel as dashed 'Awaiting' connectors. They do not count as done, and the strip says so.
D6 note
D6
Done · the month goes quiet
Done is the absence of colour. Every connector has settled into the grey fabric, and the difference track is a flat green line at $0.00 for every day of September. The only marks left are the two items carried into October (Meridian in transit, #4127 outstanding), still drawn across the cutoff because that is where they are.
The strip turns green: $0.00, adjusted bank = adjusted book = $9,029,866.58, 14 of 14. 'Complete reconciliation' becomes primary, with a summary of what was posted and who approved.
Nothing disappears: resolved items stay on the axis, and U unreconciles any of them.
D7 note
D7
Phone · the axis rotates
Is a phone version sensible? For doing the rec, no: matching needs width, ⌘-click and a keyboard. For approving, yes.
On a phone the axis rotates: time runs down, bank and books become two columns, stitches become the rungs of a ladder, and the back-dated void still reads as an arc reaching up into August.
This is Daniel between D5 and D6: two approvals, the entry he is signing, Maya's note, one big Approve. I'd ship the phone as an approval surface only.

ROUND 2 · SAME CONCEPT, LESS ON SCREEN
What I cut and why
The difference is now the headline and appears once. The axis carries shape, not words: no chip labels, no confidence pills, no legend, no key-hint bar. Labels appear only on the selected or hovered item, and confidence appears only on the selected one.
Cut: the title band, adjusted bank/book while working, the timing split in the strip (kept once, at the cutoff), line counts, journal numbers, BD3, 'n of 14' navigation, overlines, the formula table, evidence popovers, 'up next', Ember's restated findings and the tool row for a read-only search.
Kept: the stitched fabric, slants and cutoff crossings, the difference track, one reasoning line, one evidence chip, Why collapsed, Revert on each change, 'Difference →' preview where it changes a decision. Zoomed diff tracks now share the month's scale, so a nearly-done month looks nearly flat.
